title: He had everything.
paragraphs: And still… he lost his heart.

How does a man chosen by God…
end up bowing to what God hates?

How does someone who built the temple…
become a man who builds altars to idols?

A look.
A connection.
A desire you refuse to surrender.

Solomon didn’t wake up one day and decide,
“I will abandon God.”
The Bible doesn’t say he stopped loving God immediately.
It says something far more dangerous:

“For when Solomon was old, his wives turned away his heart after other gods, and his heart was not loyal to the Lord his God…”
— 1 Kings 11:4
And that’s how most people fall.
Some of us are not running from God.
We are just slowly giving pieces of our heart to things He never approved.
A relationship that pulls you away from purity.
An attachment you defend… even when the Holy Spirit is convicting you.
And here is the truth we avoid:
Whatever has your heart… has your worship.
You don’t need a golden statue to have an idol.

If it controls your decisions…
if it silences your convictions…
if it competes with your obedience to God…
It already sits on the throne.

“You shall not intermarry with them… for surely they will turn away your heart after their gods.”
— 1 Kings 11:2
But desire whispered louder than obedience.
You can be anointed… and still be vulnerable.
You can know Scripture… and still justify sin.
You can lead others… and still secretly drift.
And maybe this is where it gets uncomfortable.
Because some of you already know…
God has been speaking to you about that relationship.
That “one thing” you refuse to lay down.
But Solomon probably thought the same.
Until his heart was no longer his.
This is not where the story ends.
Because the Bible is not just a record of failure.
It is a revelation of redemption.
Where Solomon built altars to idols…
Jesus carried a cross for sinners.

“For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.”
— Romans 3:23

“But God demonstrates His own love toward us, in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.”
— Romans 5:8
Jesus didn’t wait for you to fix your heart.
He came because your heart was already broken.
And here is the hope that changes everything:
No matter how far your heart has drifted…

“If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us… and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.”
— 1 John 1:9
What has your heart right now?
Because God is not after your performance.
And He will not compete with idols.
He is not waiting to condemn you.
He is waiting to restore you.
The cross already settled your punishment.
Now grace is calling you back.
